entities.summary:
The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. is an American multinational investment bank and financial services company founded in 1869 by Marcus Goldman in New York City. Known as 'The Vampire Squid' in popular culture and widely regarded as the world's most powerful investment bank, it has historically placed alumni in top government positions globally.

Goldman Sachs revolutionized commercial paper trading in its early decades and pioneered initial public offerings, underwriting major companies including Ford Motor Company (1956) and taking Microsoft public in 1986. Its 1999 IPO ended 130 years of private partnership, raising $3.66 billion. The firm developed quantitative trading strategies that transformed financial markets, and its risk management practices became industry standards.

Goldman's role in the 2008 financial crisis — including its creation and sale of mortgage-backed securities it simultaneously bet against — became a symbol of Wall Street excesses leading to the crash. The Senate's 2010 Levin-Coburn report accused Goldman of misrepresenting securities to clients. Despite regulatory fines and reputational damage, Goldman remained a talent magnet and market-maker. Alumni include US Treasury Secretaries Robert Rubin, Henry Paulson, and Steven Mnuchin, EU head Mario Draghi, and Bank of Canada/England governor Mark Carney.
